chart_analyzer on frame_10.00.png reports a right triangle ABC with the right angle at B, identifies AC as the hypotenuse, and says segment AQ is an angle bisector with length 9; frame_12.00.png is consistent about AQ = 9 and AC being the hypotenuse.

But the only grounded numeric measurement in the retrieved frames is AQ = 9. No tool output provides any other side length, angle measure, or ratio needed to compute AC exactly, so the hypotenuse cannot be derived from the available evidence.
Therefore the supported choice is B: nan, because the current tool-grounded evidence is insufficient to determine a numeric hypotenuse length.

planner_output.refinement_instructions: Build the trace from scratch. First identify, from the retrieved frame-level evidence, the frame that clearly shows the full triangle and all relevant labels; do not assume the first retrieved frame is the correct one unless its timestamp and visibility justify it. Use OCR detections to cite exact visible numbers/text, and use chart_analyzer frame_results to map those numbers to the correct sides and confirm which side is the hypotenuse. Then compute the hypotenuse from the grounded measurements or, if the hypotenuse value is directly labeled, match that grounded value to the closest exact option. Preserve tool provenance explicitly in the rewritten trace (e.g., OCR reads ..., chart_analyzer identifies ...). If OCR and chart_analyzer disagree, prefer the frame-level result from the clearest frame and explain the mapping. Update the final answer to the option supported by the verified diagram evidence; do not guess from the options without grounded numeric labels.
